items.title: UK GDPR, Article 24: Responsibility of the controller
items.quote: Taking into account the nature, scope, context and purposes of processing as well as the risks of varying likelihood and severity
items.why: The binding UK rule on both halves of the question. Measures are scaled to the processing and its risks, and the controller must be able to demonstrate compliance and keep the measures under review. Article 30(5), read alongside, relieves organisations with fewer than 250 staff of the record-of-processing duty only where processing is occasional, low risk and without special category data.

items.title: Guidance on AI and data protection: What are the accountability and governance implications of AI?
items.locator: Section 'How should we approach AI governance and risk management?', second paragraph; section on managing trade-offs
items.quote: Your governance and risk management capabilities need to be proportionate to your use of AI.
items.why: Source of the quotation. Proportionality runs both ways: the same paragraph warns organisations not to underestimate the effort needed and requires them to demonstrate compliance on an ongoing basis. Also asks that trade-off decisions be documented to an auditable standard. The page carries the notice that the guidance is under review following the Data (Use and Access) Act.

items.title: Data protection audit framework
items.locator: Opening section and 'Who can use the framework?'
items.quote: As a general rule, the greater the risk, the more robust and comprehensive the measures you should put in place.
items.why: What the regulator's auditors use, and the successor to its accountability framework (the old address redirects here). Says there is no single approach that fits all and that the framework is for larger organisations; small businesses are pointed to simpler self-assessment resources. The page carries the notice that the guidance is under review following the Data (Use and Access) Act. No date printed; page metadata gives 10 September 2025.

items.title: A pro-innovation approach to AI regulation (white paper)
items.publisher: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
items.quote: it is important to ensure that regulatory burdens do not fall disproportionately on smaller companies
items.why: Government policy on proportionality: regulate by context and outcome, 'avoiding unnecessary or disproportionate burdens for businesses and regulators'. Policy, not law; published under a previous government.

items.title: SS1/23: Model risk management principles for banks
items.publisher: Prudential Regulation Authority, Bank of England
items.quote: should be commensurate with their size, business activities, and the complexity and extent of their model use
items.why: A UK regulator writing proportionality into the rule itself: a firm with fewer or simpler models may keep a lighter inventory and simpler tiers, and rigour inside the firm scales with each model's tier. Applies to banks with internal model approval.

items.title: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (AI Act), Article 11: Technical documentation
items.publisher: European Commission, AI Act Service Desk
items.quote: may provide the elements of the technical documentation specified in Annex IV in a simplified manner
items.why: The simplified format the criterion refers to. SMEs, start-ups and now small mid-caps may use a simplified form which the Commission 'shall establish'; an enterprise that opts for it must use that form. A provider duty for high-risk systems. No published form was found on the Commission's sites in this pass. The Commission's copy of the consolidated text; the page states it is based on the EUR-Lex consolidated version as at 27 July 2026 and marks Digital Omnibus changes NEW or AMENDED. EU law; not UK law.

items.title: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (AI Act), Article 63: Derogations for specific operators
items.publisher: European Commission, AI Act Service Desk
items.quote: without affecting the level of protection or the need for compliance with the requirements in respect of high-risk AI systems
items.why: Corrects the legacy briefing: the simplified quality management route is now open to SMEs including start-ups (not only micro-enterprises) that have no partner or linked enterprises. Paragraph 2: this does not exempt them from any other requirement, including risk management, documentation, record-keeping, monitoring and incident reporting. The Commission's copy of the consolidated text; the page states it is based on the EUR-Lex consolidated version as at 27 July 2026 and marks Digital Omnibus changes NEW or AMENDED. EU law; not UK law.

items.title: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (AI Act), Article 99: Penalties
items.publisher: European Commission, AI Act Service Desk
items.quote: The Member States shall take into account the interests of SMEs, including start-ups, and SMCs, and their economic viability when imposing penalties.
items.why: Proportionality in enforcement: for SMEs each fine is capped at the lower of the percentage and the fixed amount; the new paragraph 6a gives small mid-caps the same for the middle and lower tiers. The Commission's copy of the consolidated text; the page states it is based on the EUR-Lex consolidated version as at 27 July 2026 and marks Digital Omnibus changes NEW or AMENDED. EU law; not UK law.

items.title: AI Omnibus enters into force
items.locator: Bullets 'Support for growing companies', 'High-risk AI systems in Annex III' and 'Simplification for SMCs'
items.quote: helping more businesses benefit from a proportionate approach
items.why: The Commission's own account of the 2026 amendments: measures previously reserved for SMEs extended to small mid-caps; high-risk rules for Annex III systems apply from 2 December 2027. A news notice, not legal text.

items.title: AI Act Service Desk: Frequently Asked Questions (Digital Omnibus)
items.publisher: European Commission, AI Act Service Desk
items.locator: Question 'How will these changes benefit to businesses?' (tagged Digital Omnibus)
items.quote: making implementation easier for an additional 8,250 companies in Europe
items.why: Source of the figure. The Commission's first estimate of how many small mid-caps gain from the extension. The answer is written about the proposal ('the proposed measures'), not the adopted text, and gives no method. No date printed.

items.title: UK GDPR, Article 30: Records of processing activities
items.quote: shall not apply to an enterprise or an organisation employing fewer than 250 persons
items.why: UK law that scales a documentation duty by size and then takes most of the relief back: organisations with fewer than 250 staff are excused the record of processing unless the processing is likely to result in a risk to people, is not occasional, or includes special category or criminal-offence data. Most AI use on personal data will be regular, so the relief rarely applies. The record must be produced to the regulator on request. Personal data only; the page shows an amendment dated 30 September 2026 (the regulator is now 'the Commission').

items.title: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 (AI Act), Annex IV: Technical documentation referred to in Article 11(1)
items.publisher: European Commission, AI Act Service Desk
items.locator: Annex IV, opening words and points 1 to 9
items.quote: shall contain at least the following information, as applicable to the relevant AI system
items.why: The full list that the simplified form is a simplification of, and a ready checklist for a per-system file: description and intended purpose, design and data, monitoring and control, performance metrics, the risk management system, changes over the lifecycle, standards applied, and the post-market monitoring plan. A provider duty for high-risk systems. The Commission's copy; unlike the article pages, the annex page carries no statement of the consolidation date and shows no NEW or AMENDED marks. EU law; not UK law.

items.title: Guidance for using the AI Management Essentials tool: government response
items.publisher: Department for Science, Innovation and Technology
items.locator: Executive summary; 'Key themes and government response', Proportionality and procurement
items.quote: develop future guidance focused solely on the foundational governance measures needed to support responsible AI deployment
items.why: The most recent UK government statement on proportionate AI governance for smaller firms. Having consulted on a self-assessment tool, the department reports that smaller organisations find existing frameworks hard to navigate and that requiring the tool in procurement could burden them, and says it will write simpler guidance aimed at small and medium-sized enterprises. Limits: a consultation response (65 responses), not guidance; the tool itself remains a consultation version; the promised guidance was not found published.

items.title: Risk assessment: Steps needed to manage risk
items.locator: Sections 'What reasonably practicable means' and 'Record your findings'
items.quote: If you employ 5 or more people, you must record your significant findings
items.why: The longest-established UK model of proportionate, evidenced risk work: the effort is weighed against the risk ('You're not expected to eliminate all risks') and the duty to write it down starts at a size threshold, under regulation 3(6) of the Management of Health and Safety at Work Regulations 1999, read alongside. Shows that 'scaled and evidenced' is ordinary UK regulatory practice. Limits: health and safety at work only; says nothing about AI; cited as an analogy and where AI creates a workplace hazard.

items.title: Model Cards for Model Reporting
items.publisher: arXiv (authors' copy; Proceedings of the Conference on Fairness, Accountability, and Transparency, FAT* 2019); authors Margaret Mitchell and others
items.quote: Model cards are short documents accompanying trained machine learning models
items.why: The peer-reviewed origin of the short, structured model record: one or two pages stating intended use, performance across conditions and groups, and limits. Evidence that lean documentation is a recognised format, and something to ask a supplier for. Limits: a proposal with two worked examples, not a study of whether such records reduce harm; written by a developer's own researchers; 2019.

items.title: Closing the AI Accountability Gap: Defining an End-to-End Framework for Internal Algorithmic Auditing
items.publisher: arXiv (authors' copy; Proceedings of the Conference on Fairness, Accountability, and Transparency, FAT* 2020); authors Inioluwa Deborah Raji and others
items.quote: Each stage of the audit yields a set of documents that together form an overall audit report
items.why: Peer-reviewed framework showing how a per-system file builds up through the life of a system, stage by stage, so that decisions can be checked against the organisation's stated principles before and after deployment. Supports the top level of the criterion, where documentation withstands audit. Limits: a framework drawn from other industries, not tested for effect; designed inside a large technology company, so it needs scaling down for a small firm; 2020.

items.title: Model Artificial Intelligence Governance Framework, Second Edition
items.publisher: Infocomm Media Development Authority and Personal Data Protection Commission, Singapore
items.locator: Introduction, 'Scale- and Business-model-agnostic' (point d), p.10; paragraph 3.13
items.quote: It does not focus on organisations of a particular scale or size.
items.why: International comparator. Singapore's voluntary framework is written to be adopted in proportion: organisations of any size adopt the elements relevant to them (paragraphs 2.5 and 3.2), and document the process through a periodically reviewed risk impact assessment. Voluntary; no legal force in the UK; predates generative AI.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence Playbook for the UK Government
items.locator: Passage headed 'Auditability' (accountability and responsibility); practical recommendations on model cards
items.quote: Auditability is the process of documenting every stage of the AI innovation life cycle
items.why: Current UK government guidance on what the record is for: reporting and documentation protocols and traceability through the life of an AI project, from data collection to retirement, with model cards or fact sheets as a reference point and governance actions that are documented and proportionate. Limits: guidance for the public sector, not binding on companies.

items.title: Use of artificial intelligence in government (HC 612)
items.quote: developed to improve transparency and provide information about the algorithmic tools used in government, is not widely used
items.why: An audit finding on how far documentation lags use, even where a standard format exists: the government's own recording standard for algorithmic tools was little used when the auditor looked. A caution against assuming records exist because a template does. Limits: central government, autumn 2023 survey; the standard has since been made mandatory for departments, so the position will have moved.
